mechanism: Slide paired historical and forward date borders by a fixed step so successive in-sample windows overlap while forward windows form a continuous OOS trading history. CompareHistoryToForward maps each History DateBorders to the next non-overlapping Forward that starts at/after History.Till; parameters selected on History are then tested on Forward. Across many such pairs, stability of selected parameter sets and coefficient profiles is treated as strategy-regime robustness rather than a single-shot optimize.
data_needed: Lists of History and Forward DateBorders; per-pass ReportItem coefficients and bot params; XML Optimisation_Report with Start_DT/Finish_DT per Result
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Example Result Symbol=SBRF Splice TF=1 (M1); bot params reference USymbol=SBER; generic MT5 tester symbols/TFs
why_new_for_mis: Turns walk-forward date pairing into an explicit rolling regime-stability sensor: MIS can stream how often IS-chosen params survive the matched forward window as a change/regime-fitness channel.
quote: This approach to algorithm optimization can serve as strategy robustness testing rather than pure optimization, although it performs both roles. As a result, we can find out whether a trading system is stable and can determine optimal combinations of indicators for the system.

mechanism: For each optimization/test pass, store a VaR block on the PL series: quantiles at 90/95/99 plus Mx (mean) and Std (standard deviation). These sit beside classical PF/RF/DD in the XML Coefficients and drive SortBy/Filter on Q_90, Q_95, Q_99, Mx, Std.
data_needed: Per-pass trade PL series or precomputed Q_90/Q_95/Q_99/Mx/Std; ReportWriter.AppendVaR; SortBy flags
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: SBRF Splice TF=1 example pass; any symbol/TF the tester runs
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a pass-scoped left-tail + dispersion sensor on realized PL—not only equity DD—usable as a volatility/risk regime feature when ranking or gating strategies.
quote: VaR > 1. 90 - quantile 90 > 2. 95 - quantile 95 > 3. 99 - quantile 99 > 4. Mx - math expectation > 5. Std - standard deviation

mechanism: Break each pass’s trading results into Mon–Fri buckets (Trading_Days/Mn..Fr), each with average Profit, DD, Number Of Profit Trades, Number Of Lose Trades. Filtering/sorting can target AverageDailyProfit_* and AverageDailyDD_* per weekday, exposing which session days carry edge vs loss.
data_needed: Trades timestamped by weekday; AppendDay for MONDAY..FRIDAY; daily Profit/DD/trade counts
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same optimization passes (e.g. SBRF Splice M1); weekday aggregates independent of chart TF
why_new_for_mis: Calendar-day PL/DD profile is a lightweight intraday-seasonality / session-quality sensor MIS can use to gate strategies by weekday regime.
quote: Trading_Days - trading reports by days > 1. Profit - average profit per day > 2. DD - average losses per day > 3. Number Of Profit Trades - number of profitable trades > 4. Number Of Lose Trades - number of losing trades

mechanism: When sorting by multiple SortBy flags, compute per-metric Min/Max over the pass set; shift by |Min| if Min<0 so values lie in [0, Max+|Min|]; normalize value/Max into [0,1]; if metric is Decreasing (e.g. Std, some DD forms) use (1−value/Max); form SortBy = Σ (normalized×1/n) and OrderBy that scalar. Single-metric path uses plain OrderBy Ascending/Descending.
data_needed: IEnumerable<OptimisationResult>; one or more SortBy flags; GetSortMethod/GetSortingDirection per metric
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any report collection from MT5 optimization XML; illustrated with PF/RF numeric example
why_new_for_mis: Supplies a reproducible multi-criterion robustness score from heterogeneous signed metrics—MIS can treat the weighted SortBy as a composite health/regime score across passes or windows.
quote: the weight is equal to one divided by n (here n is the number of factor being weighted). As a result we obtain a normalized column which can be used as the sorting criteria.

mechanism: AutoFillInDateBordersM.Calculate(From,Till,historyDays,forwardDays) alternates History and Forward windows: History length=history, Forward length=forward; each new History start shifts by forward+1 days; Forward windows abut without overlap while History windows overlap. Emits List of (OptimisationType, [from,to]) for continuous walk-forward schedules.

instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol the auto-optimizer schedules; date grid in days (TF chosen separately in tester)
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes rolling IS/OOS border generation as a first-class change-detection schedule—MIS can align feature windows to the same overlapping-history / non-overlapping-forward lattice.
quote: Each new forward range must start on the next day following the previous range. Shift of historical intervals (which overlap) is equal to the step of forward windows. Unlike historic optimizations, forward ones do not overlap, and they implement a continuous trading history.

mechanism: Extend report Coefficients with SortBy.Custom filled via MQL5 TCustomFilter callback (e.g. CulculateMyCustomCoef) through AppendMainCoef(..., customCoef, ...) and OnTester return. Custom enters multifactor filter/sort with declared Ascending direction so EA authors inject any scalar sensor into pass ranking.

Loading into GUI deferred until last asset (or forced stop). Enables overnight cross-sectional robustness collection.

mechanism: Replace plain SGD weight update θ←θ−η∇L with adaptive rules during backprop: RMSprop (EMA of squared grads), AdaGrad (cumulative squared grads), Adam (bias-corrected 1st/2nd moments), AdaDelta, Nadam (Adam+Nesterov peek). Same CRegressorNets.fit path; optimizer chosen per training run; mini-batch vs SGD via batch_size.

quote: Adam has two key features; Exponential Moving Average (EMA) of Gradients… Exponential Moving Average of Moments… Suitable for Non-Convex Loss Functions… Wide Applicability

Compare optimizers by speed to plateau, oscillation, and train–val gap (e.g. SGD ~60% vs MiniBGD ~15% in article runs) as a generalization/overfit sensor for the fitted net.

why_new_for_mis: Treats the train/validation loss trajectory itself as a sensing channel for whether a neural market model remains in a stable learning regime or is diverging—usable as a model-trust gate.
quote: SGD converged faster it was close to local minima at around the 10th epoch while the BGD was around the 20th epoch, SGD converged to approximate 60% accuracy in both training and validation while BGD accuracy of 15% during the training sample and 13% on validation sample.

mechanism: Around US/EU DST switch weeks, compare last Friday M1 quote timestamp vs first Sunday/Monday quote on the broker feed. When EU and US DST states diverge, FX still closes/opens at NY 17:00 but EET labels shift; some brokers show last bar ~22:54 and first ~00:00 (missing Sunday 23:00–24:00 hour). Assumptions: close Friday NY17, open Sunday NY17, missing hour is at week open not Friday close; use gaps to infer broker server offset vs GMT without asking support.
data_needed: M1 OHLC around weekends spanning US/EU DST changes; TimeCurrent in tester; known NY 17:00 FX boundary
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1 on MetaQuotes demo; weekends Oct 2020 and Mar 2021 DST transitions; Alpari GMT+2/+3 note
why_new_for_mis: Infers broker-time regime (offset/DST policy) from observable weekend quote microstructure—critical so MIS session and calendar sensors align to true GMT/local exchange clocks in tester and live.
quote: Without having to ask the broker, we will determine its respective time shifts, so that GMT can be determined quite simply at any moment for any time stamp in the strategy tester

mechanism: Anchor FX week to New York 17:00 open (Sunday) and 17:00 close (Friday), normally 120h open / 48h closed (WeekInSec=604800; FxOPEN/FxCLOSE=61200s). Macros SoD/SoW/HoW/BoW convert any timestamp into seconds/hours within day/week so strategies can sense time-to-weekend and session position despite broker server labels.
data_needed: Broker/server datetime; GMT or inferred offset (Part 2); NY DST state; macros in DealingWithTimePart1.mqh
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex (EURUSD examples); session logic in NY local time; macros TF-agnostic
why_new_for_mis: Provides a liquidity-session clock MIS can use to gate night-scalping / London-breakout / pre-weekend flatten logic on true exchange time rather than broker bar stamps.
quote: the Forex market closes at 17:00 New York time on Friday… opens on Sunday at 17:00 New York time… normally open for (5*24=) 120 h and closed for (2*24=) 48 h.
